provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Licensed in some states; copy leans on material choice, subfloor prep, square footage and install days. No flooring or adhesive brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Solid hardwood, engineered hardwood, luxury vinyl plank, laminate and porcelain tile side by side: water resistance, pets and kids, sound, refinishing later, and how each feels underfoot
pageStructurePlus.why: Flooring buyers arrive knowing the room, not the material. They decide by comparing what survives a dog, a spill and a basement, so the comparison page does the selling.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Moisture testing on slabs and plywood, levelling compound for dips, fixing squeaks before the new floor goes down, underlayment choices and acclimation days
pageStructurePlus.why: Subfloor prep is where cheap bids cut corners and where floors fail later. Explaining it is how a careful installer justifies a higher square-foot number.

pageStructurePlus.section: Install day: tear-out, furniture and baseboards
pageStructurePlus.contains: Carpet and old tile removal and haul-away, who moves furniture and appliances, baseboard and quarter-round, door trimming, and how many days a typical room takes
pageStructurePlus.why: People put off new floors because they picture a week of chaos. A plain install-day page turns that worry into a date on the calendar.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Full sand and refinish versus screen and recoat, stain sample boards, dust containment, cure times before rugs and furniture, and when boards need replacing instead
pageStructurePlus.why: Refinishing buyers have hardwood already and ask whether it can be saved. Answering that honestly earns the refinish now and the install later.

pageStructurePlus.section: Stairs, transitions and matching existing floors
pageStructurePlus.contains: Stair treads and nosing, transition strips between rooms, thresholds at sliding doors, and weaving new hardwood into an existing floor
pageStructurePlus.why: Stairs and transitions are where an install looks finished or looks cheap. Buyers who care about those details pay for an installer who shows them.

designDirections.name: Square Foot
designDirections.bestFor: One- and two-crew installers who win on a fast measure and a clear price per square foot
designDirections.headlineSample: Hardwood and vinyl plank floors installed in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Denim and butter with geometric caps read like a measure sheet. The page drives to the free-measure form and the tap-to-call bar.

designDirections.name: Grain and Plank
designDirections.bestFor: Installers with a deep file of finished hardwood, plank and stair work to sort by room and material
designDirections.headlineSample: New floors, laid flat and finished clean, across {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Cacao keeps the warm palette with a walnut-brown accent that passes, and a bookish serif that suits wood grain.

designDirections.name: Wide Plank
designDirections.bestFor: Wide-plank, herringbone and site-finished hardwood specialists working on larger homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Site-finished hardwood and herringbone floors for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy and brass on a dark ground make honey and walnut floors glow, and the editorial serif signals craft rather than a per-foot special.

openers.line: Someone measuring their living room for new hardwood in {City} finds your Maps listing, but there's no website button, so they never see a finished floor of yours.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a flooring buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing's website link is the Facebook page. Fine for friends, but a homeowner choosing between vinyl plank and engineered hardwood wants a comparison and a measure form.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest floor they shared there.
openers.linkLine: A flooring page built for the buyer, not the feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The flooring site on your listing has a free-host banner and a contact form that didn't send when I tried it. That's the kind of thing that makes a buyer pick another installer.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a form that errors. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: Your flooring company, current and working: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your floor gallery loads sideways and the call button hides under the menu. People shopping for flooring are usually standing in the room with a tape measure.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same flooring site, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask you for a floor measure except calling. Plenty of homeowners would rather type the rooms, the square footage and the floor they're pulling up.
openers.hook: Check the listing, social pages and any site for a form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A measure request that asks for rooms, footage and the old floor: {demo-link}

openers.line: That herringbone hallway and the stair treads on your Instagram are sharp flooring work, and they're mixed in with truck and tool posts. Sorted by material, they'd close jobs.
openers.hook: Pick two finished floors on their grid you can name by material and pattern. Mention one by name if they reply.

openers.line: Your reviews mention floors with no squeaks and a crew that moved the piano back. That's what a flooring buyer wants to read, and it only lives on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about prep, cleanliness or a tricky room. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the floors they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Autumn is when people want new floors in before family visits for the holidays. The flooring installers they can find in September are the ones booked through December.
openers.hook: Use this from late August to October. Name the holiday in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the holiday flooring rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most people decide on new flooring at night with a sample board on the couch. If your only option is a phone that rings out, they message the next installer.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it's voicemail only and there is no form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A flooring estimate request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the post about hiring a floor installer. Experienced hardwood people check whether a company looks steady before they apply, same as the customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a help-wanted story. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A flooring site with a careers page for installers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You lay floors across {City} and the suburbs, but there's no page telling someone in {Neighborhood} you do hardwood there. That's the search they actually type.
openers.hook: Find the towns named in their posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A flooring page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on whole-house flooring, say it on the site. Doing every room at once is often the difference between a small job and a full install.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing in a post, a review or on the van. Otherwise skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Flooring payment options explained before the measure: {demo-link}

openers.line: Pulling up old floors can mean asbestos tile, moving appliances and working on stairs. A page showing your licence and insurance settles the first worry before the measure.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry where flooring needs a licence. Note that a record exists; never quote a number.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and prep standards on one flooring page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your flooring work comes from builders and word of mouth. That's great until a builder slows down, and even referrals search your name first.
openers.hook: Look for review or post text mentioning a builder, a designer or a neighbour. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a flooring referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the {specific recent job} on your page, tight seams and a clean transition. A stranger shopping flooring should land on that floor first.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished floor on their grid and name it exactly: material, pattern, room.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a really clean floor.

I was searching for flooring installers in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site where someone can compare materials or ask for a measure. I mocked up a sample flooring site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, circling back in case my message got lost. Here's the sample flooring site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has floors sorted by material, a hardwood versus vinyl plank comparison, and a measure request that asks for rooms and square footage. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for flooring installers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample flooring site for {Business Name}, with floors sorted by material, a measure request form and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email the link for tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many material and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a flooring company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one bedroom of hardwood."
"Could I walk you through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: I mostly work for builders, not homeowners.
objections.handler: "Then the site does two jobs: a page builders can send buyers to for upgrades, and a homeowner side for the slow months when starts dry up."

objections.objection: Customers only care about the cheapest price per foot.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones who've been burned by a floor that cupped or squeaked. Showing your subfloor prep is what makes your number make sense."

objections.objection: The flooring store sends me my installs.
objections.handler: "Good, keep that. The store sets your rate, though. Your own site gets you direct jobs where you set the price and the schedule."

objections.objection: I already pay for flooring leads.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several installers at once and you pay whether you win the floor or not. Your own site sends that homeowner to one installer, you."

objections.objection: My nephew is building me a site.
objections.handler: "Great, that's cheaper than me. Happy to share the material comparison and the measure form so he can borrow them. If it stalls, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, because it's a material gallery, a measure form and a few town pages. That's less than one room of plank."

email.subject: Flooring site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for flooring installers in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email you the link, take a look when you're off your knees. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm clearing the {Business Name} flooring demo off my server on Friday.

Want me to keep it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, it's coming up on the season when people want new floors before the holidays. Thought of you.

The flooring site is still here if you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one or two rooms of mid-range hardwood, never to an hourly rate. Installers think in square feet.
Each material page is its own line: hardwood, engineered, vinyl plank, laminate and tile each answer a different search.
A measure request that collects rooms, footage, the floor coming up and stairs is worth more than a contact form. Price it separately.
Only quote a refinishing section for installers who own sanders and actually refinish.
Builder-facing pages are a second audience. Quote them as their own line, never inside the homeowner build.
Keep town pages to towns where they have finished floors to show.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a durability comparison, room suggestions and its own gallery of finished floors in that material.

lineItems.item: Measure request with rooms and square footage
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, a stairs count, the floor being removed, a furniture-moving question and routing to two estimators.
Max when it covers each material plus tear-out, levelling and stairs as separate bands in their words.
Max with a sand-versus-recoat explainer, stain sample gallery and a cure-time checklist for the homeowner.
Max with a capacity statement, a spec-sheet download and a bid request form for production work.
Max when each town page gets its own finished floors and a review from that town.
Max when the comparison page, the price guide and the measure form are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Finished-floor photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One morning at your best finished floors, shot low with window light so the grain shows, gives the gallery and a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a floor they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile updates for each flooring job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every new floor goes on your Google profile with the material and the town, so the listing shows hardwood in {Neighborhood} last week."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once there's a finished floor to post.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review texts after the last plank goes down
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening the furniture goes back, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while they're walking around in socks on the new floor."

whatElseYouSell.name: Sample board and van artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Branded sample boards you leave with the homeowner, and van artwork that matches, so your name is on the plank they're staring at all week."

whatElseYouSell.name: Pre-holiday new floors campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A September push for new floors before the holidays fills October and November with installs instead of quotes."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Pet-owner vinyl plank landing page and ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Dog owners searching for a scratch-proof floor are a niche you can own. A vinyl plank page and a small ad run aimed right at them."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the material pages are live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Builder upgrade flyer and spec sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page flooring upgrade sheet builders hand to new buyers puts your hardwood in front of people before closing."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, for installers who already work for builders.

withoutAI.route: The flooring showroom or distributor they buy from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The flooring distributor you buy plank from sells to installers all over the metro. Introduce me and I'll build their find-an-installer page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have real budgets, and their installer list is the prospect list you'd otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.route: Home builders who sub out flooring
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The builder you lay floors for needs a site showing finished homes, and your hardwood is in every photo."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders buy marketing for model homes and lot sales. The flooring sub's introduction is a warm door.

withoutAI.whoPays: The cleaner, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Carpet cleaners hear 'we're replacing this soon' every week. They need a site, and their customers need a flooring installer's number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A two-way referral: worn carpet becomes a plank job, and the installer sends rug and upholstery work back.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every rental turnover with trashed carpet is a vinyl plank job. A turnover request page for the manager sends those to one installer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers want fast, predictable turnovers. A simple request page saves them calls and routes steady work.

withoutAI.whoPays: The mover, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Movers know which empty houses are getting new floors before move-in. They need a site, and their customers need a floor installed between closing and moving day."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Empty-house installs are the easiest floors to do, and the mover hears about them first.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Designers who spec herringbone and wide plank rarely have a decent portfolio. Yours are the floors in their best rooms, so it's an easy introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy on looks, and the installer's floors are proof for both of them.

withAI.route: Room-photo flooring visualiser for the showroom
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers upload a photo of their room and see it in three of the showroom's planks before they ever drive in."
withAI.whyItWorks: It turns online browsers into showroom visits with a shortlist, which is what showrooms sell on.

withAI.route: Turnover scope drafter for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "The manager drops in move-out photos and gets a draft flooring scope by room, ready to send to one installer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Turnover speed is the manager's money. A tool that drafts the scope gets used every week.

withAI.route: Quote follow-up for the carpet cleaner
withAI.pitchLine: "The carpet cleaner who sends you replacement jobs loses quotes to slow follow-up. Same follow-up tool you use, set up for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: It's a second build of something already working, and the introduction came from a client who trusts you.

withAI.pitchLine: "New-home buyers ask the design centre the same flooring questions. An assistant answers them from the builder's own upgrade list and books the selection."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders earn on upgrades and lose them to slow answers. The flooring sub gets the install either way.

withAI.pitchLine: "When a homeowner buys plank at the counter, the assistant asks the room count and matches them to an installer on the distributor's list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Material that never gets installed comes back as a return. Matching installers keeps the sale closed.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer describes the room and the look, and it drafts a flooring spec with species, width, finish and transitions to edit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Specs are tedious and designers bill by the hour. A small monthly tool pays for itself in one project.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for floor measure calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Can't answer with a nailer in your hand? The caller gets a text asking which rooms, the rough square footage and what floor is there now."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Flooring price calculator by material and square foot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks hardwood or vinyl plank, enters the rooms and stairs, and sees a ballpark before they ask for a measure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real price per square foot by material, tear-out and stair prices, and the minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that name the floor
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When someone reviews their new hardwood or plank, a reply in your tone is waiting for a thumbs-up on your lunch break."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review texts. Needs ten past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and material-order invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit when the flooring is ordered, balance when the last transition strip is in, each sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Room-photo floor visualiser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a photo of the living room and sees it in oak, grey plank or tile before the measure visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the material and colour list they install most, checked against real finished floors. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Measure-to-quote builder with room sketches
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sketch each room on the tablet during the measure, and the flooring quote with waste, transitions and baseboard is ready before you leave the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their quote template, waste factors by material and add-on prices.

softwareAI.name: After-hours line for flooring inquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at night, asks which rooms, the floor they want and whether there are stairs, and books the measure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, materials list and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install calendar with crew and material delivery
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every floor job on one calendar with the acclimation start, delivery day and crew, so plank isn't sitting in a garage for a week too long."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the measure form is producing. Needs their crews, typical install days per room and supplier lead times.

softwareAI.name: Moisture and subfloor log for each job
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew records moisture readings and subfloor fixes with a photo per room. If a floor ever cups, you have the record."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their prep checklist and a foreman willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Square-footage takeoff from floor plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a builder's floor plan and it drafts square footage by room, plank direction and waste for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for installers who bid builder work. Needs a few past plans with measured totals to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Acclimation and prep reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners get a text when the flooring arrives to leave the boxes in the room, and another the day before to clear furniture and turn the heat on."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their prep instructions and booking flow.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with floor selection and install date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner signs off on the plank colour, sees the delivery and install dates, and stops calling to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the install calendar in place first.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on flooring materials, pets and moisture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can I put hardwood in a basement' and 'which floor is best with two dogs' at midnight, from your own rules and materials."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their material notes and current lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Refinish reminder for past hardwood customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A few years after a hardwood install, the homeowner gets a screen-and-recoat reminder. Repeat flooring work from people who already said yes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past hardwood jobs with install dates and a recoat price.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by material and crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether glue-down hardwood, floating plank or tile actually makes you money once prep, waste and crew days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs supplier invoices and crew hours for a season of jobs.

softwareAI.name: Content writer for material and town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly drafts of pages like 'vinyl plank over concrete slabs', written from your install notes, and nothing publishes until you approve it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Builder bid tracker for production flooring
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every builder bid, lot number, upgrade selection and install window in one list, instead of texts scattered across three phones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for installers with builder accounts. Needs their builder list and how lots are scheduled.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote notes from the measure
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house, say the rooms, the floor coming up and the stairs, and it drafts the flooring quote for you to check in the van."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Distributor price-sheet sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the distributor changes plank or underlayment prices, the flooring calculator and the quote template update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the calculator. Needs the distributor's price sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for floor installers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for flooring installer and helper jobs answer your usual questions, and you only call the ones with their own tools and a ride."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and the pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the flooring calculator for every installer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built this square-foot flooring calculator for one installer. Every flooring crew in the state fields the same what-does-it-cost call."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Knowing the workflow is the hard part of vertical software. The first flooring client taught it to you and paid for it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a regional flooring distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-an-installer map on the distributor's site for every flooring crew that buys there. Installers stay with the yard that sends them homeowners."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on installer loyalty. A tool their installers live in is stickier than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified-installer program site for a flooring manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your certified flooring installers need warranty registration, install guides and a locator. I've built that workflow for an installer already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers carry warranty claims from bad installs. A program site that tracks trained installers is a budget line they understand.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member flooring contractors a site template, a measure form and a material comparison page as a benefit of joining."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew. One deal reaches dozens of flooring owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency keeps rebuilding flooring sites from scratch. License my template with the material pages and measure form built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client relationship; you sell them the finished flooring module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Turnover flooring program across a rental portfolio
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every unit you manage gets the same turnover flooring request, with standard plank specs and a fixed install window."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large managers buy once and roll out everywhere, and flooring is the biggest turnover cost they schedule.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Big-box install-partner pages for independent crews
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Crews who install for the big flooring stores need their own page for direct work. Sell them a ready flooring page with a measure form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Store installers are many, underpaid on store jobs and keen to build direct customers. A low monthly price fits them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A flooring franchise sells the same plank in a dozen territories. One template with measure requests that route by ZIP code covers them all."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New-home buyers pick flooring upgrades in a hurry. A portal with the builder's plank and hardwood options sells more and routes them to one installer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders earn margin on upgrades, and the flooring sub becomes the default installer for every lot.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Flooring material price sheet for installers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on where plank, hardwood and underlayment prices are heading, built only from price lists installers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Installers re-price jobs constantly. Built from contributed sheets, it never claims more than the sheets show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One flooring installer per metro, next metro over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A new flooring client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one flooring installer in each metro. {City} has yours, so I'm taking the flooring template to the next metro."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished-floor proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The flooring company left with a half-built site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your flooring site was started and never finished. I can launch it on a material-and-measure template that's already live for another installer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy. They need someone who can show finished flooring sites quickly.

upsellLadder.offer: Flooring site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The flooring site and the care plan go on one contract, so adding a new floor to the gallery is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review texts and Google profile updates
upsellLadder.trigger: The first floor installed since launch, with photos to post.
upsellLadder.line: "That hardwood job last week is now the first thing on your Google profile. Let's do that for every floor."

upsellLadder.trigger: They finish a floor they're proud of, or the gallery is still thin on a material they sell.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your three best floors in one morning, low and in window light. The grain sells the next job."

upsellLadder.offer: Flooring price calculator by material and square foot
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of measure requests show people asking price before booking a measure.
upsellLadder.line: "Most flooring measure requests ask the price per square foot first. The calculator answers it before you drive out."

upsellLadder.offer: Install calendar with crew and material delivery
upsellLadder.trigger: A delivery and an install day collide, or they mention a second crew.
upsellLadder.line: "That plank that sat in the garage an extra week was a calendar problem. Let's put every floor job on one schedule."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention customers who can't decide between two floor colours.
